That is the correct outcome; renaming the agent to a specialist that did not run would defeat the gate with a false record, which is the same vacuous-signal failure this packet is about. Related observation, flagged not silently rewritten: the four report.md section headings still read 'bubbles.simplify', 'bubbles.stabilize', 'bubbles.security', 'bubbles.audit' and overstate attribution in the same way. (1) SIMPLIFY -- Finding S-1, FIXED: scripts/runtime/go-integration.sh closed with two consecutive if blocks testing the identical condition, 'if [[ "$go_test_rc" -ne 0 ]]', the first echoing and the second exiting. Nothing between the two blocks can change go_test_rc, so the split was pure duplication; merged into one block with identical behaviour, and the guard suite plus the full untagged suite were re-run at exit 0. (2) STABILIZE -- no flake source found. The gate marker check is a pure string assertion over an already-captured file, with no timing dependency; a scan of the added package found no socket, no sql/pgx, no docker and no exec.Command, so a deterministic classifier over a committed YAML file cannot flake and making the lane depend on it leaves it stricter, not less reliable. (3) SECURITY -- S-1: the gate marker echoes seven distinct variables (a fixed literal prefix, three integers, two exit codes, the operator's own -run regex, and the marker line, which by construction carries only counts and two floats) and NONE is secret-bearing; zero ':-' or '-' fallback expansions exist in the changed wrapper, so it cannot print a real value. S-2: the capture file is an mktemp path at mode 600, owner-only, outside the repo tree, and removed by cleanup_gate_output on EXIT -- with the honest caveat, recorded not glossed, that trap does not fire on SIGKILL, so a hard kill could strand one mode-600 file in /tmp. Implementation-reality scan, no-stub scan, spec-match, DoD-evidence sampling and the operator-only boundary all held and no violation was found, but auditing does not certify: certification is bubbles.validate's act and validate has not re-run. The file carries ZERO //go:build directives, so it genuinely is untagged and genuinely does sit in the unit lane, which is exactly what R6.4 requires. R6.4 is SATISFIED; the check was wrong. A guard keyed on a substring that also appears in prose is the same vacuous-signal failure this bug is about, so the false positive is reported rather than quietly dropped (report.md, Audit Record A-3). rootCause: Two mechanisms with complementary intent and no link between them. tests/eval/assistant/acceptance_test.go opted OUT of the untagged unit lane via //go:build integration on the stated assumption that the tagged integration lane would pick it up. scripts/runtime/go-integration.sh selects packages by an explicit allow-list, not ./..., and was never extended to include ./tests/eval/... A build tag can only include a file inside a package that was already selected, so the opt-out executed and the opt-in did not. Nothing asserts the pairing, so the assumption printed in the file's own header went stale with no surface turning red. The failure mode of a missing test is silence.
scopeOfClaim: This gate measures assistant routing accuracy and capture-fallback coverage on an offline corpus using the harness's deterministic keyword classifier as a structural proxy for the production router. It does NOT measure corpus-grant enforcement. The D25/D28 grant holes carried by spec 108 are a separate axis and are NOT made measurable by fixing this bug.
